news.h: Visa made compulsory for six communities who came in before December 2024
news.catch: The Home Ministry amended the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order, 2025. Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who entered without valid papers on or before 31 December 2024 must now hold an “appropriate visa” to stay on.
news.why: The citizenship-versus-foreigner line, and the same 31 December 2024 cut-off that the CAA uses.

news.h: Held past 24 hours without a magistrate? You must be released, says Supreme Court
news.catch: The Court held that anyone detained beyond twenty-four hours without being produced before a magistrate is entitled to release — the constitutional clock in Article 22(2), now carried into the new criminal procedure code.
news.why: Article 22, the D.K. Basu safeguards, and the production-within-24-hours rule in the BNSS.

news.h: Census 2027: States told to flag bad data while it is still being collected
news.catch: The Registrar General and Census Commissioner has asked every State to track enumeration in real time so that “data quality concerns” are caught and corrected during collection, rather than discovered months later.
news.why: The first digital census: two phases, self-enumeration, and the 1 March 2027 reference date.

news.h: Centre may set up a panel to review the new UGC equity rules
news.catch: The Centre told the Supreme Court it may constitute a committee to review the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026, which drew objections from general-category groups and from sections of Dalit and OBC communities.
news.why: How regulations are made, how they are challenged, and what equity in admissions means.

news.h: Agniveer stays, with two more years of service
news.catch: The Defence Ministry said the scheme is not being rolled back: the service tenure has been extended by two years, and eligible recruits will be absorbed after six years.
news.why: A recruitment scheme examined through its terms rather than its headlines — a favourite CLAT move.

quiz.q: The Home Ministry made the change by amending which instrument?
quiz.e: The amendment was made to the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order, 2025, not to a statute.

quiz.q: Which community is NOT among the six named in the amendment?
quiz.e: The six are Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan.

quiz.q: The cut-off date for entry without valid documents under the amended order is:
quiz.e: Entry on or before 31 December 2024 is the dividing line — the same cut-off used by the CAA, 2019.

quiz.q: Citizenship, its acquisition and its loss, is dealt with in which Article of the Constitution?
quiz.e: Article 11 gives Parliament the power to regulate citizenship; Articles 5 to 10 fix who was a citizen at commencement.

quiz.q: The twenty-four hour rule for producing a detained person before a magistrate appears in:
quiz.e: Article 22(2) requires production before the nearest magistrate within twenty-four hours of arrest, excluding journey time.

quiz.q: Which body asked the States to track enumeration in real time for Census 2027?
o: The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
The Unique Identification Authority of India
quiz.e: The RG&CCI, which conducts the census under the Census Act, 1948, issued the direction.

quiz.q: The phase of Census 2027 in which population enumeration takes place is:
quiz.e: Census 2027 runs in two phases: houselisting first, population enumeration second.

quiz.q: The UGC regulations under review concern:
o: promotion of equity in higher education institutions
quiz.e: They are the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026.

quiz.q: Under the revised Agniveer position described in the papers, eligible recruits are absorbed after:
quiz.e: The tenure was extended by two years, and eligible recruits are to be absorbed after six years; the scheme itself was not withdrawn.
